title: Kingdom of Kakheti
capsule: The Kingdom of Kakheti was a late-medieval and early-modern monarchy in easternmost Georgia, emerging around 1466 from the breakup of the unified Kingdom of Georgia and occupying the Alazani River valley between the Greater Caucasus and the lands of Kartli. Ruled by its own branch of the Bagrationi dynasty and adhering to Georgian Orthodoxy, it survived under nominal Safavid Persian suzerainty, enduring the devastating invasions of Shah Abbas I in 1614-1617 that depopulated much of the kingdom before the dynasty was restored. Kakheti's separate existence ended in 1762, when Erekle (Heraclius) II succeeded his father Teimuraz II and united Kakheti with neighbouring Kartli to form the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of Kakheti is moderately attested from Georgian chronicles and Persian administrative records, though precise boundaries with neighboring Kartli and Safavid-controlled territories shifted repeatedly.
